ImageDescription.value: Altviolisten Kim Kashkashian en Garth Knox kozen voor een avontuurlijk programma dat puurt uit nieuw en klassiek repertoire van de twintigste eeuw. Tot deze laatste categorie behoren ongetwijfeld de duo's voor twee violen van Béla Bartók. Oorspronkelijk ontstaan als oefenstukjes kunnen deze muzikale kleinoden ook een concertpubliek bekoren. Bartók's tijdgenoot Frank Bridge is vooral bekend als post-romanticus en schilder van het Engelse landleven. Minder bekend is dat hij na 1918 resoluut de weg van Schönberg en van de polytonaliteit insloeg. Lament is hiervan een mooi voorbeeld.  De andere componisten op het programma typeren de muziekliteratuur van na 1945. Met Luciano Berio (°1925) betreden we de weg van het open oeuvre en van de transformatie van vooraf gegeven materiaal. Giacinto Scelsi (1905-1988) exploreert de klank van binnenuit in een zoektocht naar mystieke onthechting. Mystiek vinden we ook bij de Koreaan Isang Yun (1905-1995): zijn werk Contemplation verenigt westerse compositietechnieken met de geest van zen. Horatio Radulescu (°1942) en George Benjamin (°1960) tenslotte zijn beiden voorbeelden van een jongere generatie componisten die zich bewust tegen het postmoderne gedachtengoed hebben afgezet: Radulescu in zijn gebruik van klankspectra, Benjamin in navolging van zijn leermeesters Boulez en Messiaen.

ImageDescription.value: ‘Post Rotten’ is an immersive installation by the Brazilian artist Daniel Lie. For a three-day period, he will be transforming deSingel’s Small Hall into a kind of temple, a space where visitors can meet one another or simply hang out for a while. Lie will create the installation using organic material – flowers, plants, and food – in a progressive state of decay. Having grown up in São Paulo with a Brazilian mother and an Indonesian father, festive rituals are in his blood. On Friday and Saturday, he will open up his installation to performances created by and featuring Juliana dos Santos and Bruna Amaro. Lie studied visual arts with them in São Paulo, and shares a growing interest in performances in which physicality and music and/or dance play a central role. This installation and these performances are part of a broader research project entitled ‘Death Center for the Living’, which focuses on creating hybrid spaces for art, learning, spirituality and energy work.

ImageDescription.value: It may seem quite surprising, but the Croatian pianist Dejan Lazic, only 33 years old,  has been included in the circle of notable musicians for quite a while now. Take a look at his impressive record: an excellent CD recording, an unending stream of positive reviews and an overflowing concert agenda with renowned orchestras and conductors. Among them, Iván Fischer has again compiled a sparkling programme with the Budapest Festival Orchestra which we are eager to hear. Weber's 'Konzertstück' for piano and orchestra is a showcase in which to marvel at Lazics' technical mastery. With its revolutionary, fully composed structure and 'secret' programme, it was a source of inspiration for Liszt's Second Piano Concerto.  Moreover, his 'Hungarian Rhapsodies' served as template for Dvorák's 'Slavic Dances', an ode to soul of the Eastern European people, with a Slavic twist here and there. Even more national sentiment can be heard in Schumann's third and last symphony - he completed the Fourth around nine years previously -- which, quite deservedly, was called 'Der Rheinische'.

ImageDescription.value: ISCM stands for the International Society of Contemporary Music, an organisation for contemporary art music established in 1923. It is an important international network for the promotion of contemporary music and currently has around fifty members from all corners of the world. The still very young ISCM Flanders directs its attention to composers, ensembles and documentation centres as well as to everyone who is involved in contemporary music. One of the most important and annually reccurring activities is the ISCM Day, with debates on contemporary music and concerts. At this second ISCM Day, several much-lauded works from the '2007 Call for Works' are on the programme, together with compositions from the wider network of ISCM International. The performers are members of ISCM Flanders, including Spectra, I Solisti del Vento, Champ d'Action and so on.
